_comment: Position-anchor gap while disengaging: team 0's Infantry gets a plain move order (no attack target) straight through team 1's held Infantry. Team 0 stays a disengage the whole time -- never is_engaged(), never strikes back -- but team 1 is only on Hold (never chases, still defends where it stands), so it attacks team 0 one-sidedly once in range; team 0 takes real casualties, identically on main and on this fix (the casualty formula is unaffected -- only the geometry differs). Before the fix, SoldierBodies.couple() still anchored team 0's own position on the whole-block centroid (empty position_anchor_indices(), since team 0 never is_engaged()), so its kinematic advance dragged the block's slot grid straight through and past the contact-resisted bodies. After the fix, position anchors on the real contact-resisted front ranks, so the block's own advance genuinely arrests at contact instead of riding through. Clip cut off at tick 400 (well past the arrest, which is already clear by ~340): a still-commanded _move_to() that itself never yields to contact keeps pressing team 0's rear into its now-arrested front past that point, over-compressing the block -- the already-documented, deliberately out-of-scope remaining gap in docs/individual-collision-design.md's own closing note, not something new this fix introduces.
